This implies that Cabazitaxel may also interact with Tubb4a, possibly through a similar mechanism of action. The lowest common ancestor of Cabazitaxel and Eribulin is identified as a tubulin binding agent, suggesting a shared functional role in microtubule dynamics. The presence of an organic molecular entity as a common ancestor further supports a direct interaction between Cabazitaxel and Tubb4a. The evidence indicates that Cabazitaxel may exert its effects on Tubb4a via a microtubule-related pathway, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated. The strength of the evidence is supported by the hierarchical relationships and binding interactions observed, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Cabazitaxel and Tubb4a.
